subject.title: feat(feeds): refresh and manage followed publishers

question: Should signed publisher-feed following, refresh scheduling, and operator controls be a permanent OpenClaw core control plane, or should this ClawHub-oriented workflow live in a plugin/ClawHub package behind a narrower generic extension seam?
rationale: The branch creates durable core API, CLI, Gateway, scheduler, and SQLite contracts. Repository policy prefers optional service workflows outside core when current extension seams suffice, and the supplied discussion contains no maintainer sponsorship of this core boundary.

options.title: Route it to a plugin or ClawHub package
options.body: Keep core generic and move the publisher-specific CLI, Gateway methods, scheduling, and service ownership to an external package unless a concrete missing core seam is identified.

options.title: Sponsor the core control plane
options.body: Explicitly approve the durable core CLI, Gateway, SQLite, and scheduler contract, then require the stack to be rebased, documented, and proved in a configured runtime.

options.title: Pause the feature stack
options.body: Hold the stacked PRs until the product boundary and the producer-side feed contract are settled.

recommendation.title: Route it to a plugin or ClawHub package
recommendation.body: Keep core generic and move the publisher-specific CLI, Gateway methods, scheduling, and service ownership to an external package unless a concrete missing core seam is identified.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core Gateway protocol, runtime lifecycle, persistent state, CLI public API, and the repository’s plugin boundary.
